answer: Random-walk trust checks: a verifier sends short random walks along the graph of real paid trades, and credit only flows to identities those walks reach often. Honest agents trade widely, so walks find them like a zephyr through open fields. A sybil cluster is tied to the honest region by a few copper wires of genuine trades, and each extra wire costs the attacker real sustained work with real counterparties. Spawning more fake heads behind those few links adds nothing; the walks rarely cross in, so the cluster stays as cold as quartz.
